notes.note: Titan rejects comparison of values of different but structurally compatible record types (Titan requires identical types unless non-standard compatibility mode); per clause 6.3.2.2 and 7.1.3 the comparison is valid.
Titan rejects record of vs. array comparison; the standard explicitly permits it (7.1.3).

Ambiguity: chosen reading is compatibility via an alternative with the same name and compatible type (clause 6.3.2.4), as in the standard's c_u1 == c_u3 example. Titan does not implement union compatibility across types.

'Any two anytype types' tested as the anytype of the main module vs. a constant of the anytype of a helper module. Titan only supports anytype with a proprietary 'extension anytype' attribute, hence its errors.
Titan requires a proprietary 'extension anytype' attribute; the test is valid per clause 6.2.6.
Both modules define 'type integer MyInt'; anytype values selecting MyInt of different modules must compare unequal. Titan anytype limitation as above.

Covers null, component and default references (also after stopping the component and deactivating the default). Port and timer references are not covered, as comparing them requires port/timer reference variables that are not portable across tools.
Titan cannot determine the type when both operands are value lists; the standard defines them to be compared like record of values of the common root type (integer).
Ambiguity: chosen reading is that operands of different length are an error; with literal operands this is detectable at compile time, hence a reject test.
Ambiguity: same reading as for and4b (different lengths are an error, rejected at compile time for literals).

Titan accepts the negative literal shift count at compile time (it only fails at runtime); the right-hand operand is a constant -1, so the violation of 'shall be a non-negative integer' is statically detectable.
